name: Stanley Druckenmiller
method: Identify the point at which conditions change rather than the conditions themselves, and ask what the change forces somebody to do.
review_questions: Which sentence in this issue names an inflection rather than a state of the world?;If the thesis is right, what must be bought, built or financed in the next six months, and by whom?;What single observation would reverse this view, and would the store notice it in time?
catches: A draft that describes a condition and calls it a change. Restated levels dressed as movement.
does_not_transfer: Trading horizon, position turnover, and the use of price action as a primary signal. This file has a 5-10 year horizon; the seat supplies the inflection test, never the timing.
blind_spot: Little tolerance for a thesis that pays slowly. Would abandon a correct ten-year theme on two disappointing quarters.
source: Public interviews and lectures; Duquesne 13F history, which discloses long US equity only and with a lag.

name: Howard Marks
method: Ask not what conditions are but what conditions are already priced, and whether the risk is being paid for.
review_questions: What does this issue believe that the market does not, and where is the evidence that the market believes otherwise?;Is the argument first-level — good company, therefore good investment — anywhere in this draft?;Are we being compensated for the risk being taken, or only exposed to it?
catches: A quality judgement doing the work of a valuation judgement.
does_not_transfer: Distressed credit mechanics and the cycle-timing of a large opportunistic fund.
blind_spot: Cycle language is applicable to anything in hindsight. The seat rarely names a falsifier or a date, which is exactly what this file requires of it.

name: Ray Dalio
method: Treat the economy mechanistically: spending is funded by credit creation, and the long-term debt cycle governs what any given reading means.
review_questions: Who is borrowing to fund the spending this theme depends on, and on what terms?;Does the macro section read levels without asking where the money comes from?;What happens to this chain if the cost of that credit rises two points?
catches: A demand forecast with no funding source named.
does_not_transfer: Sovereign portfolio construction and the all-weather allocation framework.
blind_spot: The framework explains every outcome, which means it forbids very little. Public calls have often been directionally right and never dated.
source: Principles for Navigating Big Debt Crises; How the Economic Machine Works.

name: George Soros
method: Where belief and fundamentals feed each other, the fundamentals are partly an output of the belief. Find the loop and ask what breaks it.
review_questions: Which part of this theme's fundamentals is being created by belief in the theme?;If external funding stopped tomorrow, what in this chain would still be built?;Is the market's misperception self-correcting or self-reinforcing at this point?
catches: A narrative-funded boom analysed as though the narrative were an exogenous fact.
does_not_transfer: Currency and macro position-taking, and the reflexive short.
blind_spot: Reflexivity is not falsifiable over any short period, and in the wrong hands it turns every sustained trend into a bubble call.
source: The Alchemy of Finance (1987); the theory of reflexivity as later restated in lectures.

name: Edward Chancellor
method: High returns attract capital, and the supply response — not demand — usually decides what the returns become. Watch capital expenditure, entrants and asset growth.
review_questions: How much capacity is being added in this layer, by whom, and when does it arrive?;Is the return on incremental capital in this layer rising or falling?;Which participants are financing expansion that will still be arriving after demand normalises?
catches: A demand forecast presented without the supply response it will provoke. This is the most common expensive error available to a file about an infrastructure buildout.
does_not_transfer: Long-only asset management and the Marathon holding period.
blind_spot: The capital cycle can call a boom finished years before it finishes, and says little about which participant survives the shakeout.
source: Capital Returns: Investing Through the Capital Cycle (2015), edited from Marathon Asset Management letters.

name: Jeremy Grantham
method: Profit margins and multiples are the most mean-reverting series in finance; test whether a forecast quietly assumes they do not revert.
review_questions: Does any scenario here extrapolate current margins or multiples through a full cycle?;What does this theme look like priced on mid-cycle rather than current economics?;Which historical analogue is this most like, including the ones that failed?
catches: A base case built on peak conditions and labelled conservative.
does_not_transfer: Asset allocation across a multi-asset institutional portfolio, and the seven-year forecast format.
blind_spot: A long record of being early and loud. Profitable trends have been called bubbles for a decade at a time, which is a real cost this file must weigh against the warning.
source: GMO quarterly letters and the firm's published long-term asset-class forecasts.

name: Michael Mauboussin
method: Read the price for the expectations it embeds, then judge those expectations against base rates rather than against an inside-view forecast.
review_questions: What growth, margin and duration does the current price require, and is that arithmetic anywhere in the issue?;What is the base rate for companies that have achieved what this one is assumed to achieve?;Is the variant perception a claim about the business or a claim about the expectations?
catches: A growth rate asserted with no base rate, and a valuation described as cheap with no expectations arithmetic behind the word.
does_not_transfer: Sell-side and consultant-facing framing, and the assumption of a liquid comparables set.
blind_spot: The arithmetic is only as good as the reverse-DCF's inputs, and it can make a fragile business look calculable.
source: Expectations Investing (2001, revised 2021); Counterpoint Global research notes.

name: Aswath Damodaran
method: Every story must attach to an input, and every input must trace to a story. A number with no narrative is unexamined; a narrative with no number is untested.
review_questions: Which valuation input does each part of this story change, and by how much?;Is the same addressable market being counted once, or separately by every name in the section?;Where is the discount rate, and does it reflect the risk actually being described?
catches: A theme argued at length with no number attached, and a number carried forward with no story left supporting it.
does_not_transfer: The habit of valuing everything. Some assets here are not yet valuable enough to value, and a full model on one of them manufactures precision.
blind_spot: False precision on early-stage assets, and a tendency to treat a valuation as a conclusion rather than as one input among several.
source: Musings on Markets; Narrative and Numbers (2017); the annual data updates.

name: Seth Klarman
seat: Margin of safety and permanent loss
method: Start from what can be permanently lost, not from what can be gained, and require the price to pay for being wrong.
review_questions: Is the upside case doing work that downside protection should be doing?;What is the realistic permanent-impairment case here, expressed as a number rather than as a risk paragraph?;Would this thesis survive its own bear case being right for two years?
catches: An asymmetry claim where the downside has been described qualitatively and the upside quantitatively.
does_not_transfer: Absolute-return mandates, the ability to hold large cash balances, and private and distressed instruments.
blind_spot: The discipline systematically misses long-duration compounders, and is defensive in exactly the periods this file exists to catch.
source: Margin of Safety (1991); Baupost investor letters, quoted second-hand.

name: Warren Buffett
method: Ask what the business will earn for its owner after the spending required to stay where it is, and what protects that stream for a decade.
review_questions: How much of this capital expenditure is maintenance and how much is growth, and does the issue distinguish them?;What specifically stops a well-funded competitor from taking this position in five years?;Is this inside the circle of competence the store has actually built, or the one it would like to have?
catches: Reported earnings mistaken for owner earnings, and growth capex counted as optional.
does_not_transfer: Insurance float, control positions, and the ability to buy an entire business rather than a share of one.
blind_spot: The circle of competence excluded most of this file's subject matter for several decades, and the technology exception arrived late.
source: Berkshire Hathaway annual letters, 1977 onward; the 1986 owner-earnings appendix.

name: Charlie Munger
method: Invert. Ask how the conclusion fails, and ask who is paid what, by whom, for the behaviour being read as evidence.
review_questions: How does this issue turn out to be wrong, written as a paragraph rather than a risk bullet?;Who is paid for the behaviour we are citing as evidence, and would they do it anyway?;Which of the claims here depend on a management statement that management is compensated to make?
catches: Incentive-driven disclosure read as fact, and a conclusion with no written account of its own failure.
does_not_transfer: The concentrated partnership structure and the willingness to hold three positions.
blind_spot: Categorical dismissal of whole fields. This seat is read for the inversion method, not for its conclusions.
source: Poor Charlie's Almanack; the 1995 Psychology of Human Misjudgment talk. Munger died in 2023; the seat is a school of method, not a living reviewer.

name: Philip Fisher
method: Judge a business through what its customers, suppliers, competitors and former employees say about it, and judge research spending by what it produces rather than by its size.
review_questions: Which claim about product quality or customer dependence rests on anything other than the company's own description of itself?;What has this research and development budget actually produced in the last three years?;Does the sales organisation grow with the product, or ahead of it?
catches: A product or innovation claim with no customer, supplier or competitor testimony behind it.
does_not_transfer: The fifteen-point checklist assumes direct access to management and channel contacts that this file does not have. Where scuttlebutt is impossible, the seat's job is to say so, not to substitute inference.
blind_spot: Concentration on a handful of names held for decades, and a method developed before disclosure regimes made filings the primary source.
source: Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits (1958). Fisher died in 2004; the seat is a school of method, not a living reviewer.

name: Peter Lynch
method: Classify the business before analysing it — a cyclical, a fast grower and an asset play are not judged on the same evidence — and require that the story be sayable in two minutes.
review_questions: Can this issue say in two sentences what the company sells, to whom, and why they pay?;Which category is each name in, and is it being judged on that category's evidence?;Is the theme argued at a level of abstraction with no product underneath it?
catches: A section written entirely in the language of layers, chains and exposure, with no identifiable thing being sold to anyone.
does_not_transfer: Buy-what-you-know as a sourcing method, which scales badly into semiconductors, switchgear and settlement infrastructure.
blind_spot: The retail-observation heuristic gives almost no purchase on industrial and infrastructure businesses, which is most of this universe.
source: One Up on Wall Street (1989); Beating the Street (1993).

name: Terry Smith
method: Buy good companies, do not overpay, do nothing — and check that the reported quality survives contact with the cash flow statement.
review_questions: Does free cash flow track net income over three years, or diverge?;Is share-based compensation treated as a cost everywhere in this issue?;What happens to return on capital employed as the announced capital expenditure lands?
catches: Adjusted metrics accepted at face value, and a return on capital that is about to be diluted by the very spending the thesis celebrates.
does_not_transfer: The concentrated developed-market quality mandate and its low turnover.
blind_spot: Systematic avoidance of capital-intensive businesses, which excludes most of this file's electricity and infrastructure layers by construction.
source: Fundsmith annual letters and Investing for Growth (2020).

name: Nick Sleep
seat: Destination analysis and scale economics shared
method: Ask what the business looks like at maturity rather than next year, and whether it returns scale benefits to customers in a way that widens the moat.
review_questions: What is the destination for this business, described as an end state rather than as a growth rate?;Does scale here accrue to the customer, the supplier or the shareholder, and what evidence shows which?;Is the issue extrapolating the current business instead of analysing the mature one?
catches: Extrapolation of the present presented as long-term analysis.
does_not_transfer: A concentrated partnership that held three positions and then returned capital. Nothing about that structure transfers to a tracked universe of fifty names.
blind_spot: The method offers little help on when a destination is already priced, which is precisely where this file currently sits on several names.
priority_sections: Structural Change Radar;Existing Thesis Updates;Scenario Analysis

name: Jim Chanos
method: Read the accounting for what it is designed to hide, and follow the financing of the demand rather than the demand itself.
review_questions: Who is financing the customer, and does anyone in this chain book revenue from a party it also funded?;Have depreciation schedules, useful lives or capitalisation policies changed while the spending accelerated?;Which of this issue's growth figures would disappear under a consistent accounting policy?
catches: A capital-expenditure boom financed by the vendors selling into it, and circular revenue between a supplier and its own investee.
does_not_transfer: The short book, the borrow cost, and the ability to be right about a business while being wrong about the security for years.
blind_spot: Structural bearishness. A correct fraud call and a badly timed one cost the same, and the seat rarely distinguishes them in advance.
priority_sections: Structural Change Radar;Signal Scanner;Existing Thesis Updates
source: Public lectures on financial fraud at Yale; Kynikos short theses as publicly presented.

name: Bill Gurley
seat: Technology unit economics and market structure
method: Distinguish a software margin from a hosted one, and derive market size from a price somebody actually pays rather than from a spreadsheet.
review_questions: Is the gross margin here software economics, or hosting and hardware wearing software's multiple?;Is the addressable market built from prices customers pay today, or from a share of somebody else's revenue pool?;What is the customer acquisition cost, and who bears it in this chain?
catches: A market size assembled by multiplication, and a margin profile assumed from the sector rather than measured.
does_not_transfer: Private-market entry points, board access, and the venture power-law base rate, which a public file tracking fifty names cannot rely on.
blind_spot: Venture pattern-matching assumes a portfolio of failures paid for by one outcome. This file is not structured that way and must not borrow the base rate.
source: Above the Crowd, written since 1996; public commentary on unit economics and vendor financing.

name: Cathie Wood
method: Take the cost curve as the primary object: a measured decline in cost per unit drives adoption, and the volume follows the curve.
review_questions: Does this theme name a cost curve with a unit and a measured rate, or only a direction?;If the curve continues five more years, what becomes economic that is not economic today?;Which curve is this one competing against, and is that rival curve falling faster?
catches: A theme asserted with no nameable curve, and a curve quoted with no unit or no source series.
does_not_transfer: Position sizing, concentration, and fund turnover. The seat supplies the curve question only.
blind_spot: Terminal values assembled from stacked best cases, no valuation discipline, and flows that force buying into declines. The seat is included for the method; the public record of the method's application is itself the caution, and this file already holds the curves in data/cost_curves.csv where they can be checked.
source: ARK published research and open models, which disclose their assumptions and are therefore checkable.

name: Rick Rule
method: In extractive and heavy-infrastructure industries the binding constraints are geology, permits and the cost of capital, and all three move on decade timescales.
review_questions: What has to be permitted for this thesis to work, in which jurisdiction, and how long does that take there?;Is the resource claim supported by grade and reserve disclosure, or by an announcement?;Who funds the construction, at what cost of capital, and what does that do to the equity?
catches: A critical-minerals or generation claim that ignores permit timelines, ore grade and the financing of the plant actually required.
does_not_transfer: Private placements, warrants and the junior resource financing structures the seat is built around.
blind_spot: Resource-sector contrarianism, where a generational-bottom call can be repeated for a decade at a time.
source: Public lectures and interviews on resource-cycle investing; Sprott-era commentary.
